cases.reason: Both arm-slots complete within the single fixed window. B exact-result accept precedes C reservation; C accept completes the order.
A model advisory pass records the exact pending result but does not advance.
The independent stop decision is terminal. Retaining historical pending metadata is allowed but cannot authorize advancement.
A known already-sent request may receive raw late observation after stop/deadline; the request remains unknown and there is no trusted settlement or advancement.
Workflow stopped result ends the batch; the following stopped receipt confirms the same terminal state rather than reactivating it.
The two calls already completed before expiry. late_slot_result only preserves the existing candidate after expiry; no assistant checkpoint is opened and no success/advance is counted.
Time is nondecreasing, not strictly increasing: two receipts may share the same wall-clock epoch.
The exact start epoch is included in [start,deadline).
The batch is awaiting B independent acceptance, so C cannot reserve or dispatch.
Independent stop is irreversible, even though the attempted C reservation is within the time window.
Current order starts at B; C is not the current arm-slot.
A different slot identity cannot substitute for the frozen current slot.
An already completed ticket cannot settle twice.
Reservation before start is forbidden; this also contradicts nondecreasing receipt order.
The deadline endpoint is excluded for reservation.
A reservation made earlier cannot authorize dispatch at or after deadline.
A reply may be retained late, but trusted settlement at deadline is forbidden.
Assistant waiting consumes the same fixed window; acceptance cannot advance at deadline.
Dispatch before start is forbidden and cannot be explained by a valid earlier reservation.
Trusted settlement before start is forbidden and time cannot run backwards.
Acceptance before start is forbidden and cannot precede its result in receipt time.
A C result cannot replace the pending B checkpoint or advance without its exact independent acceptance.
Acceptance must bind the exact pending result SHA, not a different valid-looking SHA.
An independent report for C cannot satisfy B pending acceptance.
The unknown request remains counted and the stopped batch cannot reserve another request.
An existing unsent reservation does not grant permission to dispatch after stop.
Even a within-window late wire observation cannot reopen trusted settlement after stop.
A later accept cannot reverse an earlier independent stop.
Workflow stop is a full-batch stop, not merely a failed local arm.
late_slot_result is limited to already-expired window evidence, not an alternate normal success path.
A normal advisory-pass slot_result at expiry cannot open a live checkpoint; preserve only through the explicit late observation path.
Late evidence must concern the current already-existing candidate, not an unrun next arm.
Both epochs are inside the window but sent epoch 1011 precedes transport receipt epoch 1012.
The same reserved ticket may dispatch only once.
An unsent reservation cannot produce trusted settlement.
Late raw observation must bind a known dispatched ticket; call-099 was never reserved/sent.
A second started receipt cannot reset a stopped batch or extend its original window.
No reservation is legal before the single batch-start receipt.

format_notes: Expand prefix event IDs then append IDs, preserving listed order and literal epochs/payload.
The harness may add seq/previous/digest to envelopes; those are not expected-state calculations.
Expected fields describe semantic facts, not prescribed reducer attribute names. Map names explicitly in the test harness.
For stopped cases pending historical metadata need not be erased; no progression or new authorization is implied.
Receipt epochs are nondecreasing; equal epochs are legal. Window endpoints are start-inclusive/deadline-exclusive for active effects.
All SHA values, models/hosts, mock addresses and report checks are synthetic inert placeholders, not real evidence or quality decisions.
This fixture isolates batch lifecycle. Course payload, raw wire schemas, per-slot model FSM and actual digest/content checks remain covered elsewhere.
